perspective:
Arthur Chung’s available information:

- He knows he is working with Teresa on a community service project involving tasks such as medical supplies and patient records.
- He observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed; he becomes concerned for her well-being and believes she needs help.
- He offers to help. He hears Teresa say she can manage but that there is a lot to do; then she accepts help organizing medical supplies. He agrees and starts helping.
- Afterward, Arthur believes Teresa is hesitant to accept help because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathetic and tries to reassure her that accepting help does not undermine her ability. He hears Teresa say she appreciates it, wants to show she can do it herself, and agrees she sometimes needs reminding.
- Later, Arthur believes Teresa is still struggling. He feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results and wants to support her without making her feel inadequate. He tells her she is doing a great job and proposes they work together rather than him simply helping her. He hears Teresa say it has been a busy day, she feels behind, and working together could help.
- Arthur believes the collaborative approach will ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He feels hopeful and commits to it. He arranges that he will handle inventory while Teresa manages patient records, and they will check in regularly. He hears Teresa agree it feels less overwhelming and that she is glad they are working together.
- By the end, Arthur believes their teamwork paid off and strengthened their professional relationship. He feels satisfied and intends to continue the collaborative approach in future projects. He hears Teresa agree, call it a great experience and a fantastic idea, and thank him for being a supportive colleague.

He does not have access to Teresa’s unspoken private thoughts, narrator-only assessments, or any details about her that were neither observed nor told to him.
